premise: Choosing to test his polio vaccine on himself and his own family before mass trials.
hook: Before giving his vaccine to millions of children, he injected his own wife and children with the live virus.
key_facts: Developed the first successful polio vaccine in the early 1950s.
Opted to use a killed-virus approach rather than a live-attenuated one, sparking fierce scientific debate.
Refused to patent the vaccine, famously asking 'Would you patent the sun?'
Field trials in 1954 involved over one million schoolchildren.

premise: Rising from a humble yak herder and porter to reaching the summit of Mount Everest for the first time.
hook: He failed on six previous Everest expeditions over two decades before finally reaching the top.
key_facts: Born in Tibet and raised in Nepal as part of the Sherpa community.
Worked extensively as a high-altitude porter for British and Swiss Himalayan expeditions.
Reached the summit of Mount Everest alongside Edmund Hillary on May 29, 1953.
Later became the first director of field training at the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute.

premise: Enduring the public humiliation of his groundbreaking astrophysics discovery by a leading British astronomer.
hook: A top scientist publicly ridiculed his mathematical proof on a ship voyage to England, setting back black hole physics by decades.
key_facts: Calculated the maximum mass a white dwarf star can hold before collapsing, known as the Chandrasekhar limit.
Was publicly dismissed by Sir Arthur Eddington at a Royal Astronomical Society meeting in 1935.
Continued his research in isolation at the University of Chicago for decades.
Awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1983 for his work on stellar evolution.

premise: Overcoming severe poverty and hair loss to build a multi-million-dollar beauty empire.
hook: She suffered from a severe scalp ailment that caused her to lose most of her hair before inventing a formula that changed her life.
key_facts: Born Sarah Breedlove on a Louisiana cotton plantation in 1867, the first child in her family born free.
Started her hair care business in St. Louis with just a few dollars of savings.
Employed a vast network of door-to-door sales agents known as 'Walker agents'.
Recognized by Guinness World Records as one of the first self-made female millionaires in America.

premise: Stepping inside a cramped Vostok capsule to become the first human to orbit Earth despite unknown physiological risks.
hook: Doctors had no idea if a human would go blind, lose their mind, or die from weightlessness in outer space.
key_facts: Selected from a group of 20 elite Soviet fighter pilots for the Vostok 1 mission.
Completed one orbit around Earth on April 12, 1961, lasting 108 minutes.
Ejected from the capsule as planned and parachuted safely down to Russian farmland.
Became an international celebrity, touring globally to promote Soviet space achievements.

premise: Financing and filming his debut masterpiece over three years through endless financial collapses.
hook: He shot his film entirely on weekends whenever spare cash arrived, pausing production whenever the money completely ran out.
key_facts: Worked as a commercial graphic designer in Calcutta before turning to cinema.
Pawned his wife's jewelry and sold his own book collection to fund initial shooting for 'Pather Panchali'.
Released 'Pather Panchali' in 1955, winning Best Human Document at the Cannes Film Festival.
Received an Academy Honorary Award in 1992 for his lifetime contribution to cinema.
